What to judge: `manifestStandsOver` now lets a closed scope's sealed manifest stand over a dependency of another project that moved with the consumer's trust pin, through `externalDependencyStands`. The dependency must keep its ref, identity and relationships, be resolved and done then and now, and keep its plan digest and governing contracts. It must also have a current review bundle, and no blocker of the current manifest may name it. When that holds, its revision, digests, evidence, implementation digest and review id are taken from the current manifest. The trust policy digest follows only when at least one such dependency moved. Judge whether the kept fields are the right definition of "the same commitment". Check whether a moved dependency could carry a change the closed scope's reviewer should see (for instance a done spec whose requirements changed without its plan digest changing). Check whether the current acceptance really proves current trust and an approved review of the dependency, and whether a same-project dependency is untouched. Measured on harne8 with pose-dist at edcf5f2: `closeout-check spec:harne8-abm-governed-execution` is terminal=false with edcf5f2 and terminal=true with this change; its three pose-dist dependencies had only follow-up dispositions recorded and been reviewed again.

Do NOT run `pose assess`, `pose state`, `pose index` or anything else that writes under `.pose/`; dispose assess-* tools from the sealed evidence and the code. Leave the worktree as you found it. If you build or test Go code, let every `go test` finish (do not interrupt it) so the toolchain removes its own build directories. Dispose the `validate` tools from the sealed evidence: the pipeline ran `pose validate --strict` on a clean clone of the sealed commit with a GitHub token (`.pose/results/delivery-validation.json`); a rerun in your sandbox fails for environment reasons and is not evidence about the code. For `artifact-check` and `surface-check`, build the engine of this subject (`go -C pose-mcp build -o "$TMPDIR/pose" ./cmd/pose`) and run that binary, not a `pose` from PATH. A finding object accepts exactly `id`, `severity`, `disposition`, `file`, `line`, `summary`, and for an accepted follow-up `action`, `owner`, `review_by`; put any rationale inside `summary`. A new finding's id carries no round prefix (F1, F2, ...). This is round 1: `prior_findings` is empty. Sweep the whole surface and report every finding in one pass, classified blocker vs follow-up.

Since round 1: `externalCommitmentUnchanged` reads the dependency spec at the sealed and the current revision in its own project and requires the same text before its Final Report (only the Final Report, where follow-ups are disposed, may differ; an unreadable revision is a change), and `TestAMovedFederatedPinWithChangedRequirementsStales` uses a real git repository with a changed requirement and the same plan digest.
